title: South Africa holds its first non-racial national election
summary: South Africa’s 1994 election opened national voting across racial categories. The country commemorates 27 April as the milestone of its first democratic, non-racial election.

citations.note: Supports the factual summary and chronology. Context includes explicitly interpretive comparisons; the date note identifies limits of precision.

claims.text: South Africa’s 1994 election opened national voting across racial categories. The country commemorates 27 April as the milestone of its first democratic, non-racial election.
Commemorative election date; voting extended over several days.
The election marks a political transition, not the end of every legacy of apartheid. A commemorative day should also be distinguished from the full voting period.
